intro: Many travelers skip insurance — until something goes wrong. A motorbike accident or sudden illness in Thailand can mean high bills at a private hospital. The right cover keeps you safe and stops a small problem becoming a financial one.

blocks.html: Short answer: Always get travel insurance for Thailand. The biggest reason is medical cost — especially motorbike accidents, which are common among tourists. Private hospitals are good but expensive for serious cases. Choose a policy that covers medical treatment, emergency evacuation, and the activities you will actually do (including motorbike riding and diving).

blocks.title: Read the motorbike exclusions
blocks.html: This is where claims fail most often. Many policies only pay for motorbike-accident treatment if you held a valid license and wore a helmet. Confirm this clearly before you ride.

faq.q: Do I need travel insurance for Thailand?
faq.a: It is not legally required for ordinary tourists, but it is strongly recommended because serious medical care at private hospitals can be very expensive — especially after motorbike accidents.

faq.q: Does insurance cover riding a motorbike?
faq.a: It depends on the policy. Many only pay if you held a valid license and wore a helmet. If you plan to rent a motorbike, choose a plan that clearly states it is covered.

faq.q: How much medical cover should I get?
faq.a: Pick a limit high enough for serious cases and emergency evacuation, especially if you are heading to islands or doing adventure activities. Too low a limit may not cover surgery or several days in hospital.
